public_rationale: The September 19, 2024 SCoRe study documented models correcting their own mistakes without external error judgments at inference time, including occasional correction within a single response [e1]. This provides a counterexample to the categorical denial of self-checking before August 12, 2025 [e1]. DeepSeek’s January 22, 2025 report also described spontaneous verification and reflection [e2]. Earlier experiments published October 3, 2023 found failures of intrinsic self-correction, limiting confidence in its reliability without negating the later demonstrations [e1, e3].
limitations: SCoRe used specialized training; its results do not establish that every model checks every answer [e1].
The DeepSeek evidence is developer-reported and does not establish general reliability [e2].
Demonstrated self-correction does not imply dependable error detection across tasks [e1, e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs do not sanity check their own work.

statement.excerpt: They do not sanity check their own work.
statement.document_title: LLMs are not like you and me—and never will be.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is a categorical denial that LLMs examine their own reasoning or responses for mistakes.
A counterexample must show actual checking or correction, rather than merely a claim by the model that it checked.
Checking need not be infallible. An external verifier supplying the correction does not qualify by itself.
Assess capabilities demonstrated by 2025-08-12. Earlier demonstrations remain relevant to this categorical capability claim; no lower time bound is asserted.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evaluations of contemporary LLMs, including reasoning models, show no genuine inspection or correction of their own work without externally supplied error judgments.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented pre-post LLM examines and corrects its own reasoning or response without an external error judgment at inference time.

evidence.explanation: SCoRe evaluates correction without external feedback at inference time and documents revision of the model's own mistakes. It supplies a behavioral counterexample, although the models received specialized training; the event date denotes the capability documented by publication.

The report describes the model spontaneously revisiting earlier reasoning during generation. This supports the existence of self-checking, although the developer's report does not establish its general reliability; the date is when this capability was publicly documented in the cited version.
